claim: In reasoning LLMs, self-consistency exhibits lower initial discrimination and lags behind verbalized confidence under moderate sampling budgets, though both signals improve (scale) with more samples.
stance_target: self-consistency is always the strongest black-box uncertainty signal regardless of sample budget
scope_conditions: 3 reasoning models, 17 tasks spanning mathematics, STEM, humanities; no code-generation tasks
quoted_support: Both self-consistency and verbalized confidence scale in reasoning models, but self-consistency exhibits lower initial discrimination and lags behind verbalized confidence under moderate sampling.

claim: A hybrid estimator combining self-consistency and verbalized confidence with just n=2 samples improves AUROC by up to +12 points on average and already outperforms either signal alone even when that signal is scaled to much larger sample budgets, after which returns diminish.
stance_target: most of the achievable uncertainty-quantification gain is front-loaded at very low sample counts, supporting cheap/low-n proxies over expensive full sampling
scope_conditions: 3 reasoning models, 17 tasks across math, STEM, humanities
quoted_support: Most uncertainty gains, however, arise from signal combination: with just two samples, a hybrid estimator improves AUROC by up to $+12$ on average and already outperforms either signal alone even when scaled to much larger budgets, after which returns diminish.

claim: Sample-scaling and signal-complementarity effects for uncertainty estimation are domain-dependent: mathematics (the native domain of RLVR-style post-training) shows higher uncertainty quality and stronger, faster-scaling complementarity between signals than STEM or humanities domains.
stance_target: generality of self-consistency/verbalized-confidence scaling behavior across domains
scope_conditions: mathematics vs STEM vs humanities, reasoning models with RLVR-style post-training
quoted_support: These effects are domain-dependent: in mathematics, the native domain of RLVR-style post-training, reasoning models achieve higher uncertainty quality and exhibit both stronger complementarity and faster scaling than in STEM or humanities.

claim: This paper studies only black-box, fully verbalized/self-consistency signals under extended chain-of-thought reasoning and does not evaluate code-generation tasks or internal-state-based (white-box) single-pass probes, leaving both a code-domain gap and a white-box-signal gap.
stance_target: coverage limits of current sample-scaling studies relative to the AAAI-27 code-LLM cheap single-pass angle
quoted_support: We study parallel sampling as a fully black-box approach using verbalized confidence and self-consistency. Across three reasoning models and 17 tasks spanning mathematics, STEM, and humanities, we characterize how these signals scale.
